content.comment_body: Hello, I am interested in understanding the life cycles of the internal flash memory in [article_no]. Is it possible to download a program from a PC to an SD card and run it directly from the card, rather than writing to the internal flash memory, to extend its lifespan?

I'm not clear about your concern. The program memory in [product_name] is only overwritten when the program or parameters are changed. There are devices in use for many years without memory issues. If you save your program on a micro SD card, the program will still be loaded into the program memory whenever the device restarts. I don't have information about the exact number of write cycles, but you can reach out to [company_name] support for further details by submitting a Support Request.

Yes, I'm aware the memory is only written during programming (and during power-off cycles for certain items), but I'm using it for educational purposes, and the unit will be reprogrammed many times daily.
In that case, it's best to submit a Support Request as previously mentioned.

You must store your user program within [product_name] itself; execution from the micro SD card isn't possible. The process for storing retentive data isn't documented, but it's likely kept in internal RAM and only saved to fixed memory during power-down. Based on current knowledge, there have been no significant issues with memory life in such cases.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is concerned about frequent reprogramming impacting the lifespan of flash memory in [product_name]. The main question is whether programs can be run directly from an SD card instead of using internal flash memory. Replies clarify that the device cannot execute directly from an SD card—on each restart, the program is transferred from the SD card to internal memory. The exact write cycle limits are not published, but there are no common reports of problems. It is suggested to contact [company_name] support for official information.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to reduce wear on internal flash memory either by limiting program writes or executing software from an SD card. They seek clear information on memory endurance and the limits of write cycles.
